successors.name: Roman Empire
successors.text: Acarnania, which after Actium in 31 BCE became part of the Roman province of Achaea; Augustus removed the inhabitants of several towns to Nicopolis

ledger.x: 314: Cassander reorganises the Acarnanian League 'on a truly federal basis'.

c. 250: Acarnania is partitioned. 'partitioned between Aetolia and Epirus in, c. 250 BC'; the League page has the Acarnanians and Aetolians make peace 'in ca. 270 BCE' after Pyrrhus's death and agree 'the Acheloos River as their mutual border', the south 'incorporated into the Aetolian League'. The two pages differ by…
c. 250 (or ca. 270): 'the northern part with Leucas went to Epirus'; Acarnania page: 'partitioned between Aetolia and Epirus in, c. 250 BC'.

c. 189 (bridge): the southern part returns. The Acarnania page says only that 'the river Achelous formed the boundary between Acarnania and Aetolia' under the Romans or a little earlier; no page opened dates the Aetolian loss of Stratos and Oeniadae. 189 is the Roman reduction of the Aetolian League on the…
168: after Pydna Rome takes Leucas from the League.

wars.name: Second Macedonian War
wars.outcome: The Acarnanians were 'forced to capitulate to the Roman Republic'.

wars.name: Roman-Seleucid War
wars.outcome: The Acarnanians 'were persuaded by their countryman Mnasilochus to espouse' Antiochus's cause in 191; no loss of land is on the page.
